correctness.rationale: The discriminant is primitive and linear in c, hence irreducible. The explicit repeated-root map b=-a lambda, c=lambda^3+a lambda^2 is finite (lambda integral) and birational (lambda=-b/a over a != 0) into a normal polynomial ring. Over R=k[a,c], B has free basis 1,lambda,lambda^2 and A has submodule basis 1,a lambda,a^2 lambda^2; multiplication by b preserves it. Multiplication by lambda and lambda^2 forces a^2|h0 and a|h1, hence conductor a^2 B=(a,b)^2A. Differentiating Delta gives -ab^2,-a^2b,-a^3 and the relation b^3=a^2 b^2-a^3 c, yielding J=(a,b)^3. Reducing a=0 gives c=lambda^3, purely inseparable of degree three. The extracted SymPy checker passed; all universal statements rest on the proof, not finite samples. Boundary outside the monic chart is not claimed.

value.rationale: The universal cubic discriminant is a canonical irreducible singular variety, and characteristic three is the first modulus in which its generic repeated-root cover has a Frobenius degeneration. Computing the precise conductor as the square of the singular-line ideal, the intrinsic Jacobian as its cube, the normalization quotient torsion orders (1,2), and the purely inseparable conductor cover gives a complete structural description of distinct natural singularity invariants. The point is the contrast between normalization defect and infinitesimal critical scheme, not an arbitrary numerical example, routine reparameterization, or merely code verification. No unsupported downstream applications are claimed.
